credentials.description: API key from the Wave Business portal (sent as Authorization: Bearer); it is tied to a real wallet — Wave documents no sandbox

example_prompt: Add a Wave recipient check before sending a payout.

mobile.description: Recipient's phone number in E.164 format. e.g. "+221700000000".

name.description: Expected recipient name. If provided, Wave returns name_match indicating whether the name matches.

national_id.description: Expected national ID document number. Returns national_id_match if provided.

amount.description: Planned payout amount. If provided, Wave returns within_limits indicating whether the recipient can receive this amount.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code. Required if amount is provided.

within_limits.description: true if the recipient can receive the requested amount. null if amount was not provided.

name_match.description: Result of the name comparison (Jaro-Winkler algorithm, threshold 0.65). NAME_NOT_KNOWN if the recipient is not KYC-2. null if name was not provided.

national_id_match.description: Result of the ID document check. null if national_id was not provided.

code.description: Error code. e.g. too-many-requests if the limit of 30 checks per 5 min is exceeded.

details.description: Validation details returned on request-validation-error. Each entry contains loc (field location), msg (message), type (error type). Can be null or absent (measured on 2026-10-24 on 401 errors) — check before iterating.

gotchas: Rate limit: 30 checks including a name comparison (name field provided) for the same number within a 5-minute window. Beyond that, this number is blocked for 60 minutes. Calls without name are not subject to this limit.
NAME_NOT_KNOWN does not mean that the name is incorrect — it means that Wave has no legal information on this recipient (not KYC-2). Do not block a payout on that basis alone.
The name comparison uses Jaro-Winkler with a 0.65 threshold — minor spelling variations (accents, abbreviations) can return MATCH.
national_id_match requires specific activation by Wave. Without this activation, the field always returns null even if national_id is provided.

If the API key was created with request signing (optional Business Portal setting), every call must carry Wave-Signature: t={timestamp},v1={HMAC-SHA256(timestamp + raw body)} computed with the signing secret (format wave_sn_AKS_…, shown only once) — empty body for a GET. Without it: 401 missing-signature; other codes: invalid-signature, invalid-signature-format, invalid-signature-timestamp, expired-signature-timestamp (timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past or more than 30 seconds in the future). The setting is permanent for a key: to drop it, revoke the key and create another one.

[MUST TELL USER] The API IP whitelist turns on as soon as the first address is added in the Business Portal (Developer section) and can no longer be turned off from the portal — you have to go through your Wave account manager. Calls from an unlisted IP get 403 ip-not-allowed: on hosting without a fixed outbound IP (serverless functions, most PaaS), do not add any IP before you have a fixed egress.
